bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to "Miles City Field Office Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan Amendment".
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution opens certain land administered by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) in eastern Montana to coal leasing. Specifically, it nullifies the rule issued by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) relating to the Record of Decision and Approved Resource Management Plan (RMP) Amendment for the Miles City Field Office in Montana. The BLM approved the RMP Amendment on November 20, 2024. The RMP Amendment made no acres available for coal leasing and 1,745,040 acres unavailable for further consideration for coal leasing to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a Bureau of Land Management decision for eastern Montana that closed roughly 1.7 million acres to future coal leasing. If enacted, the resolution would nullify that closure and reopen the land to potential coal leasing. The BLM had closed the area in November 2024 to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly reopens land to coal leasing, affecting coal extraction companies' access to federal mineral resources.
Coal mining operations would regain the ability to lease and develop mineral resources on the affected acreage.
Coal-fired power generators could be affected by changes in domestic coal supply availability from these federal lands.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would open certain land administered by the federal land agency in eastern Montana to coal leasing.
plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what may be done with that land. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
